Meanwhile, state‑run media reports that the Ministry of Energy is attempting to ration electricity and accelerate the deployment of renewable projects, though progress remains slow. Ordinary Cubans are reportedly struggling to keep lights on, heat their homes, and power essential appliances, with some turning to makeshift solar setups or borrowing from neighbors to survive the day.

As Washington continues to tighten its economic pressure, the Cuban administration faces mounting domestic pressure to resolve the energy crisis while maintaining its political stance. The situation underscores the fragile intersection of international sanctions and domestic resilience, leaving the island’s population to navigate a day‑to‑day reality marked by uncertainty and scarcity.
author: France 24

title: Turkey employs drones to detect and combat wildfires
content:
Turkey’s emergency services are increasingly deploying drones to combat the country’s frequent wildfires. The unmanned aircraft, equipped with infrared and high‑resolution cameras, can survey large forested areas in real time, identifying heat signatures that are invisible to the naked eye. By spotting fires at an earlier stage, the technology enables rapid dispatch of firefighting teams and reduces the time required to locate and assess new blazes.

The initiative follows a series of severe wildfire seasons that have strained Turkey’s firefighting resources and highlighted gaps in early detection. According to a France 24 report, the drones are integrated with existing satellite feeds and ground‑based sensors, creating a layered monitoring system that improves situational awareness. Operators can zoom in on hotspots, track fire spread, and relay precise coordinates to crews, thereby improving coordination and minimizing damage to both natural habitats and nearby communities.

While the drones are still being refined, preliminary trials have shown a measurable reduction in response times and a higher rate of successful containment of small fires. As Turkey continues to invest in this technology, the hope is that it will become a standard component of the nation’s wildfire management strategy, enhancing both safety and environmental protection.
author: France 24

title: South Korea football association apologises over sexual services allegations
content:
The English Football Association (FA) issued a formal apology on Thursday after it was revealed that the governing body had circulated inaccurate claims concerning the qualification processes for the 2014 FIFA World Cup and the football tournament at the London 2012 Olympic Games. The statements, which suggested irregularities in the selection of teams and alleged undue influence over match outcomes, were later found to be unfounded, prompting the FA to acknowledge the error and retract the comments.

In its apology, the FA said the misinformation stemmed from a misinterpretation of internal reports and pledged to strengthen its communication procedures to avoid similar incidents. The association also confirmed that all qualifying matches for both the World Cup and the Olympic tournament were conducted in accordance with FIFA and International Olympic Committee regulations, and it will cooperate fully with any further inquiries. The apology aims to restore confidence among stakeholders and reaffirm the FA’s commitment to transparency and integrity in football governance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rashid Khan leads Afghanistan to 92-run ODI win over Ireland
content:
Afghanistan secured a 92‑run victory over Ireland in the second One‑Day International of their five‑match series, with leg‑spinner Rashid Khan spearheading a dramatic collapse of the Irish batting line‑up. After posting a competitive total, Afghanistan’s bowlers tightened the reins, and Khan’s incisive spell produced a flurry of wickets that dismantled Ireland’s chase, leaving them well short of the target.

The win gives Afghanistan a 2‑0 lead in the series and places them in a commanding position as the contest moves forward. With the remaining three matches still to be played, both sides will look to adjust strategies, but Afghanistan’s combination of solid batting and Rashid Khan’s match‑winning bowling will be a key factor as they aim to clinch the series.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Phone book helps locate former Syrian spy chief in hiding
content:
A joint operation by Syrian intelligence agencies and international partners culminated this week in the capture of a man known locally as “The Spider,” a former militia commander who earned a reputation for brutal tactics during the country’s civil war. The operative, identified as 48‑year‑old Abdulrahman al‑Hussein, was apprehended in the town of Al‑Karak, near the Turkish border, after a year‑long investigation that combined satellite surveillance, intercepted communications, and a network of informants embedded in rebel-held territories.

Investigators traced al‑Hussein’s movements by analyzing encrypted messages that referenced a series of covert supply routes used to transport weapons and fighters across the Euphrates. Interrogations of captured militants revealed that “The Spider” oversaw a series of extrajudicial killings and forced disappearances in the Aleppo province between 2013 and 2017, actions that earned him the moniker among locals. The operation’s success hinged on a coordinated effort between the Syrian Ministry of Interior, the United Nations’ Monitoring Group on Syria, and a European forensic team that matched DNA evidence from recovered victims to al‑Hussein’s known relatives.

Al‑Hussein is now in custody pending formal charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Authorities say the arrest sends a clear signal that individuals responsible for severe violations will be pursued despite the passage of time, and they intend to use the case to bolster broader reconciliation and accountability initiatives across Syria.
author: BBC World

title: Somosierra Prepares for Solar Eclipse Visitors
content:
Somosierra, a high‑altitude plateau in the Sierra de Guadarrama, will serve as a prime viewing point for a total solar eclipse on the evening of 12 August. The event, which will sweep across northern and eastern Spain and the Balearic Islands, is the first total eclipse visible in the region in more than 120 years. Local authorities warn that the influx of visitors and the need for temporary infrastructure will pose significant logistical challenges, prompting calls for coordinated crowd management and emergency services.

The landscape around Somosierra is marked by wind‑blasted peaks, dry grasslands grazed by cattle, and an abandoned aerodrome that once hosted generations of glider pilots. The airfield’s flat runways, once a training ground for pilots who harnessed thermals, now lie silent beside flocks of vultures and red kites that patrol the skies. The eclipse will temporarily eclipse this quiet, drawing thousands of spectators to witness the rare celestial alignment.

As the sun’s corona becomes visible and the sky darkens, the region will experience a brief period of totality lasting only a few minutes. While the event offers a unique opportunity for both amateur astronomers and the general public, the expected surge in visitors underscores the need for careful planning to ensure safety and preserve the natural and historical integrity of the area.
author: Guardian Science

title: Hardware Backdoors Detected in Certain x86 CPUs
content: A new open‑source project, **rosenbridge**, was posted on GitHub by user *xoreaxeaxeax* and subsequently surfaced on Hacker News. The repository, located at https://github.com/xoreaxeaxeax/rosenbridge, offers a lightweight utility for bridging ROS (
author: Hacker News

title: US plans $1 billion aid package for Colombia after de la Espriella inauguration
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump publicly praised de la Espriella, describing him as a “smart, strong, and tough leader” in a statement released by the White House on Thursday. The comment was made during a briefing on the administration’s ongoing diplomatic outreach, in which Trump highlighted the importance of strong leadership among the United States’ international partners.

The compliment was directed at de la Espriella, a senior political figure who has held prominent positions in his home country’s government. The president’s remarks were part of a broader effort to reinforce bilateral ties and underscore shared priorities, according to officials familiar with the discussion. No further policy actions were announced in conjunction with the statement.
author: Euronews

title: Iran uses AI-enhanced murals and posters as visual propaganda in US conflict
content:
Tehran at War (Part 2/2) – France 24 reports that Iran’s confrontation with the United States now extends to a massive visual campaign, with the state commissioning thousands of large‑scale posters and murals across the capital. These artworks, placed on public walls and rooftops, serve as billboards that broadcast the government’s official narrative, aiming to reinforce domestic support and project Iran’s perspective to an international audience. The program, which began in the aftermath of the 1979 Islamic Revolution, has been continuously refined to align with the regime’s political objectives and to counter perceived foreign propaganda.

According to the French broadcaster, recent iterations of the campaign incorporate artificial‑intelligence tools that accelerate design, translation, and distribution, allowing messages to be rapidly updated and tailored for both Persian‑speaking citizens and foreign viewers. The AI‑enhanced posters feature stylized imagery of national symbols, slogans denouncing U.S. policies, and references to historic revolutionary themes, creating a cohesive visual language that links past revolutionary rhetoric with contemporary geopolitical tensions. France 24 concludes that the state‑sponsored mural strategy illustrates how Iran leverages modern technology to amplify its diplomatic messaging and sustain a narrative that extends beyond its borders.
author: France 24

title: Family watches Birmingham Phoenix vs Welsh Fire Hundred match at Edgbaston
content:
A family outing to Edgbaston on Saturday afternoon turned into a local sports event as the Birmingham Phoenix faced Welsh Fire in the men’s Hundred. The match, held at the historic ground, ended in a decisive victory for the visitors, with the hosts struggling to keep pace throughout the innings. Earlier that day, the Phoenix women had secured a win, providing a contrasting highlight for the venue’s supporters.

The game attracted a mixed crowd, including families who followed the action from the stands. Among them was a young fan who, despite initial restlessness, was encouraged by the atmosphere and received a pair of foam meerkat paw stickers and a large red‑and‑orange Phoenix flag as a souvenir. The gesture, offered by a volunteer, helped maintain the child’s enthusiasm for the sport despite the team’s loss.

The event underscores the community role of cricket in the region, drawing both seasoned supporters and new fans alike. While the Birmingham Phoenix’s performance fell short, the match offered a platform for local engagement and family participation, reinforcing the sport’s appeal to a broad audience.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ewan and Ewen Murray Discuss Case of Mistaken Identity
content:
Guardian journalist Ewan Murray and Sky Sports golf commentator Ewen Murray were recently embroiled in a case of mistaken identity that sparked a brief but intense backlash from fans. The confusion began when an angry email circulated in early 2011 from a disgruntled Arizona fan who wrote, “I don’t know what it is like in your country, sir. But here in America we SPIT!!!” The message was mistakenly addressed to the Guardian’s Ewan Murray, but it was actually intended for the Sky Sports commentator. The misdirected rant was amplified when the commentator’s live commentary on a Tiger Woods incident in Dubai—where Woods was seen emptying his mouth on a putting surface—was taken as criticism of the Guardian journalist.

The mix‑up led to a wave of frustration from “canteen commandos” and other fans who believed they were confronting the wrong Murray. Social media threads and online forums quickly filled with calls for clarification, and the Guardian’s editorial team issued a brief statement confirming that the two individuals are unrelated and that the email had been misdirected. The incident underscores the importance of accurate attribution in the age of rapid online communication, especially when two professionals share a name and operate in overlapping media circles.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Man City Sign Rulli From Marseille
content:
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Argentine goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli from Olympique de Marseille, completing a deal that will see the 31‑year‑old join the Premier League club on a free transfer. Rulli, who has been a regular in Marseille’s backline since 2019, will replace the departing goalkeeper in the City squad, with the move officially announced on Monday.

The transfer, which involved no transfer fee, was agreed after City’s coaching staff evaluated Rulli’s experience in both Ligue 1 and international competition, noting his strong shot‑stopping record and composure under pressure. Rulli will join the squad ahead of the 2026‑27 season, adding depth to a goalkeeping department that has been a focus of the club’s recent recruitment strategy. He is expected to compete for the number one spot and provide a reliable backup option.

With the deal now finalized, City’s management expressed confidence that Rulli’s arrival will enhance the team’s defensive stability. The Argentine will report to training next week, where he will begin integrating with the club’s first‑team setup and preparing for the upcoming campaign.
author: BBC Sport

title: EFL Cup's Wildest Scorelines
content:
BBC Sport has highlighted some of the most dramatic moments the EFL Cup has delivered in recent years, as the tournament prepares to launch its new season. The analysis, released ahead of the opening fixtures, catalogues matches that have stunned fans with lopsided scorelines and unexpected twists, underscoring the cup’s reputation for unpredictability.

The review points to a handful of standout games: a 9‑0 rout of a lower‑division side by a Premier League club, a 7‑1 thrashing that saw a top‑flight team break its own record for most goals in a single cup match, and a 6‑5 thriller that ended in a penalty shoot‑out after extra time. It also notes the occasional “giant‑killer” upset, such as a Championship side defeating a Premier League giant in a 3‑2 win, and the 5‑4 comeback that saw a team overturn a 2‑0 deficit to win on penalties. These examples illustrate the cup’s capacity for high‑scoring, high‑stakes drama that keeps supporters on edge.

With the new season’s fixtures announced, the EFL Cup is poised to deliver more surprises. BBC Sport’s coverage promises to keep fans informed of the latest upsets, record‑breaking performances, and the ever‑present possibility that any match could produce a headline‑making scoreline.
author: BBC Sport

title: Newcastle's Jaissle to Lead First Friendly vs Valencia
content:
Newcastle United announced that Matthias Jaissle will take charge of the club’s first pre‑season friendly against Valencia, marking the start of a new era for the Magpies. The appointment follows the dismissal of former head coach Eddie Howe, and Jaissle’s arrival signals a shift toward a more modern, data‑driven approach.

Jaissle, who previously managed Bayer Leverkusen in Germany’s Bundesliga, will oversee the 2–0 match at St James’ Park on 30 July. The fixture, part of Newcastle’s preparation for the upcoming Premier League season, will test the new coach’s tactics and squad cohesion against a technically proficient Spanish side.

The game is expected to provide a benchmark for Jaissle’s integration into the club and a preview of the style he intends to bring to Newcastle. A positive result could boost confidence ahead of the first competitive fixtures, while the experience will inform his subsequent training and selection strategies.
author: BBC Sport

title: Silver Nanocatalyst Switches Reaction Sites for Power Generation and Hydrogen Production
content:
Researchers have identified that a silver (Ag) nanocatalyst functions at distinct reaction sites within solid oxide cells depending on whether the device is operating in power‑generation mode or as a hydrogen‑producing electrolyzer. The discovery, made by a multidisciplinary team, shows that the same catalyst can adapt its active sites to the differing electrochemical demands of each mode, a behavior not previously documented for nanocatalysts in solid oxide technology.

The study demonstrates that during electricity generation the Ag nanocatalyst preferentially facilitates oxygen reduction reactions at specific lattice sites, whereas in hydrogen production it shifts to sites that favor water oxidation and hydrogen evolution. This mode‑dependent site selectivity suggests that catalyst architecture can be tuned to optimize performance for each application. By designing cells that exploit these dual‑site capabilities, engineers can potentially reduce catalyst loading, lower operating temperatures, and extend component lifetimes.

The finding introduces a new design principle for next‑generation solid oxide cells: tailoring nanocatalyst site distribution to the intended operating mode. If applied in commercial devices, this approach could improve energy efficiency and cost‑effectiveness for both power generation and hydrogen production, accelerating the deployment of solid oxide technology in the broader energy transition.
author: Phys.org

title: Teen Cannabis Use Linked to Slower Cognitive Development
content:
Teenagers who begin using cannabis may experience a deceleration in the development of key cognitive functions, according to recent research. The study found that memory, attention, language, and processing speed—areas that typically improve steadily during adolescence—tended to plateau in users while non‑users continued to show gains.  

The findings suggest that the onset of cannabis use does not immediately impair cognition but can alter its trajectory over time. Researchers identified tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) as the most likely contributor, particularly in relation to declines in memory performance. The data indicate that early exposure to THC may interfere with the normal maturation of neural circuits involved in these cognitive domains.  

These results underscore the importance of monitoring adolescent cannabis use and its potential long‑term effects on brain development. Further investigation is needed to clarify the mechanisms involved and to guide public health recommendations.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Achieve Quantum Entanglement Using Sunlight
content:
Scientists have demonstrated that quantum entanglement can be generated directly from sunlight, offering a lower‑energy alternative to the high‑power lasers traditionally used in quantum experiments. In an outdoor setup, researchers illuminated a specially designed crystal with natural solar radiation and measured the resulting photon pairs. The entangled photons exhibited a fidelity of approximately 94 % relative to an ideal Bell state, indicating that the sunlight‑derived entanglement is highly coherent and suitable for practical use.

The experiment underscores the feasibility of harnessing ambient light for quantum information tasks, potentially simplifying the hardware required for quantum satellites and ground‑based communication links. By eliminating the need for bulky laser systems, the approach could reduce launch mass and power consumption for space‑borne quantum platforms, while also enabling more energy‑efficient quantum computing architectures that rely on entangled photon sources. The high fidelity achieved in this first outdoor demonstration suggests that further refinements could bring sunlight‑generated entanglement to the threshold required for secure quantum key distribution and other quantum networking protocols.
author: Science Daily

title: Nitecore Releases Lightest 10,000mAh Power Bank
content:
Nitecore has launched the fourth generation of its NB10000 ultralight power bank, targeting users who prioritize minimal weight and size in portable charging solutions. Priced at $83.95, the device offers a 10,000 mAh capacity while weighing 146 grams, according to measurements taken by reviewers. The manufacturer’s specifications list dimensions of 1.45 × 11.6 × 4.68 cm (0.57 × 4.57 × 1.84 in), positioning it as the most compact and lightweight model in its capacity class currently available on the market.

The NB10000 Gen 4’s reduced mass and compact form factor are intended to appeal to backpackers, bikepackers, and trail runners who seek to minimize the load of ancillary gear. Reviewers have noted that the power bank’s size and weight represent a significant reduction compared with previous generations and competing products, potentially allowing users to carry a high‑capacity charger without compromising overall pack weight. The product is now available for purchase, with further details published in a review by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: U.S. Announces $1 Billion Security Aid for Colombia as New President Takes Office
content:
The U.S. State Department announced late Friday that the Trump administration will provide $1 billion in security assistance to Colombia, coinciding with the inauguration of the country’s new president, Abelardo De la Espriella. The funding is part of a broader U.S. effort to support Colombia’s counter‑insurgency and drug‑trafficking operations.

De la Espriella, who introduced himself as “The Tiger,” took the oath of office at a military garrison in Cali and pledged to “defeat narco‑terrorists” in his first speech. His campaign focused on strengthening the armed forces, intelligence capabilities, and law‑enforcement cooperation with neighboring states. The U.S. aid package is intended to bolster these initiatives, providing equipment, training, and logistical support to counter the influence of drug cartels and related violent groups.

The announcement underscores Washington’s continued commitment to Colombia’s security and stability, while signaling a willingness to invest in the nation’s efforts to curb narcotics trafficking and insurgent activity. The assistance is expected to enhance Colombia’s operational capacity and reinforce the bilateral partnership between the two countries.
author: France 24

title: Three killed in Russian missile strike near Kyiv as Zelensky visits Serbia
content:
Russian missile strikes on Saturday killed three people, including a child, in Ukraine’s Kyiv region, local authorities said. The attack occurred just hours after President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Belgrade for a landmark visit to Serbia, a nation that maintains close ties with Moscow. Ukrainian officials confirmed the casualties but did not immediately identify the type of missile or the specific target of the strike.

France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze reported from Kharkiv that the incident adds to a series of recent attacks on civilian areas across the country, underscoring the ongoing security challenges Ukraine faces even as it pursues diplomatic outreach. While the Kremlin has not commented on the specific strike, the timing of the attack coincides with Zelensky’s efforts to strengthen ties with regional partners, highlighting the complex interplay between military actions and diplomatic initiatives in the conflict.
author: France 24

title: Typhoon Dolphin strikes southern Japan and moves toward China
content:
A powerful typhoon has swept across Japan’s southern islands, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and widespread disruption. Meteorological agencies reported that the storm intensified as it moved over the Pacific, prompting emergency alerts and prompting authorities to mobilize rescue teams throughout the affected prefectures.

The storm caused dozens of injuries, with local hospitals treating victims of wind‑related accidents and flooding. Power outages were reported across multiple municipalities, leaving thousands without electricity and prompting temporary shelter arrangements for displaced residents. Transportation networks, including rail and road services, experienced significant delays as debris and landslides obstructed key routes.

The typhoon is now tracking northeast toward China, where officials have pre‑emptively closed several major ports to mitigate potential damage to maritime infrastructure and cargo operations. Preparations include reinforcing flood defenses and positioning emergency response units along the projected path, as authorities monitor the system’s strength and projected landfall.
author: DW World

title: Brandon Clarke death ruled accidental, heroin and cocaine involved
content:
Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke, 27, was found dead on May 11, and the Tennessee medical examiner’s office has ruled the death accidental. The autopsy report cites the combined effects of heroin and cocaine as the primary factors, and officials confirmed that no foul play was involved. Toxicology tests revealed significant levels of both substances in Clarke’s system, leading investigators to conclude that the overdose was unintentional.

The Grizzlies released a brief statement expressing sorrow for Clarke’s family and friends while noting that the organization is cooperating fully with authorities. Team officials emphasized that the findings underscore the importance of ongoing efforts to address substance‑abuse issues within the professional sports community. Clarke’s death adds to a growing list of accidental overdoses among athletes, prompting renewed discussions about health and support resources for players.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Footballers' Families Must Relocate Quickly During Transfer Window
content:
During the summer and winter transfer windows, footballers’ families often find themselves in a state of flux, with last‑minute deals forcing rapid relocations that can span hundreds of miles. The sudden nature of these moves means that households must quickly arrange housing, school placements for children, and employment for partners, all while the player negotiates contracts and medicals. Agents and club officials typically coordinate logistics, but the emotional toll on families—especially those with young children—remains significant, as they must adapt to new neighbourhoods, cultures, and support networks in a compressed timeframe.

Clubs now recognise the importance of a smooth transition for players’ families, offering relocation packages that cover temporary accommodation, visa assistance, and educational support. In many cases, the clubs’ community outreach teams liaise with local schools and employers to secure suitable arrangements, while player unions provide counseling and financial planning advice. Nevertheless, the unpredictability of transfer negotiations can still lead to abrupt changes, leaving families to juggle packing, moving, and settling in new environments often with little notice.

Despite these challenges, many families report that the professional support structures in place help mitigate the upheaval. The ability to secure a stable living situation quickly and to maintain continuity in children’s schooling or partners’ careers is seen as crucial for a player’s performance and well‑being. As the football calendar continues to demand rapid transitions, clubs and governing bodies are increasingly investing in comprehensive relocation programs to ensure that the human side of the sport remains as resilient as the on‑field talent.
author: BBC Sport

title: Greenland Issues Warning Over Trump‑Linked Oil Firm’s Unapproved Drilling Plans
content:
Greenland’s eastern coast has become the focus of a new dispute after the arrival of drilling equipment from Greenland Energy, an American oil company linked to former U.S. President Donald Trump. Officials from the island’s government have stated that no formal approval has been granted for the company’s exploratory activities. The equipment, reportedly intended for the installation of wells, was brought ashore in recent days, raising concerns among local authorities about the legality of the operation.

The company’s presence comes amid heightened U.S. interest in Arctic resources, with the president repeatedly asserting claims over the region’s vast oil and gas reserves. Greenland Energy’s plans to sink wells in remote parts of the island have not been coordinated with the national regulatory framework, prompting officials to question the company’s compliance with environmental and permitting requirements. The situation remains unresolved as the government seeks clarification on the company’s intentions and the status of any necessary permits.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Wildfire smoke raises respiratory problems and mortality concerns in Canada
content:
Scientists are racing to untangle the complex links between wildfire smoke exposure and mortality as fire weather becomes increasingly common across Canada. In the spring of 2024, a series of intense fires in northern Ontario’s boreal forests sent plumes of soot and ash across the country, turning Toronto’s skyline into an “almost post‑apocalyptic” orange haze. The event has prompted a surge of research into how prolonged exposure to fine particulate matter and other combustion by‑products affects human health, especially in densely populated urban centers.

Erin O’Connor, chief of the emergency department at Toronto General Hospital, reported a noticeable uptick in patients with allergies, asthma exacerbations, and short‑ness of breath during the smoke episode. “It really hit you in the face as soon as you walked outside,” she said, noting that even inside the hospital the air carried a distinct burning scent. Hospital air‑filtration systems were activated to protect vulnerable patients, but the sheer volume of particulate matter forced many to seek medical attention. Researchers are now collecting clinical data, air‑quality measurements, and demographic information to model dose‑response relationships and identify high‑risk groups.

The growing body of evidence underscores the urgent need for public health interventions and policy measures to mitigate wildfire smoke impacts. By refining exposure‑mortality models, scientists hope to inform early warning systems, improve air‑conditioning standards, and guide emergency response protocols. As climate‑driven fire events are expected to rise, understanding these connections will be critical for protecting population health and reducing wildfire‑related morbidity and mortality.
author: Guardian World

title: Infantino Gains South American Football Backing at Colombian Inauguration
content:
Gianni Infantino, the FIFA president, appeared at the inauguration of Abelardo de la Espriella as the new president of CONMEBOL, where he received strong support from South American football officials. The ceremony, held in Quito, Ecuador, marked a new chapter for the continent’s governing body, which has faced criticism over governance and corruption in recent years. De la Espriella, a former FIFA executive, was elected on a platform of transparency and reform, and Infantino’s presence underscored FIFA’s commitment to working closely with CONMEBOL to address these issues.

During the event, Infantino thanked South American stakeholders for their confidence and pledged continued collaboration on development projects, including youth academies and infrastructure improvements across the region. The partnership aims to streamline coordination between FIFA and CONMEBOL, ensuring that reforms are implemented and that the continent’s national teams receive adequate support for upcoming international competitions. The inauguration, attended by representatives from 12 member associations, signals a renewed focus on accountability and growth within South American football.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Violence forces displacement of Palestinian Christians in Gaza, Jerusalem and West Bank
content:
Palestinian Christians in Gaza, Jerusalem and the occupied West Bank are experiencing a surge of violence and forced displacement, according to reports from local NGOs and international observers. In recent weeks, churches and Christian neighborhoods have been targeted by clashes between Israeli security forces and Palestinian protestors, with several incidents of property damage and physical assaults documented in Gaza’s Rafah and Khan Younis, as well as in East Jerusalem’s Christian Quarter.

The displacement crisis has intensified as families flee from areas of heightened conflict, citing fear of ongoing raids and the threat of further attacks. Humanitarian groups estimate that more than 3,000 Christian residents have left their homes in the West Bank, while in Gaza, at least 1,200 families have sought refuge in temporary shelters. These movements mirror a broader trend of Christian communities feeling increasingly vulnerable amid the broader Israeli‑Palestinian conflict, which has seen a rise in targeted violence and restrictions on movement.

International human rights monitors have called for an immediate end to the violence and for the protection of minority communities. They emphasize that the displacement of Christian families not only exacerbates humanitarian needs but also threatens the cultural and religious diversity that has long characterized the region. The situation remains fluid, with ongoing calls for dialogue and security guarantees to prevent further harm to these communities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bangladesh rules out Shakib Al Hasan's return to cricket
content:
Shakib Al Hasan, Bangladesh’s premier all‑rounder, announced that he is prepared to return to his home country to face the pending legal proceedings, provided that the authorities guarantee his personal safety. The cricketer, who has been residing abroad since the charges were filed, said the assurance would enable him to attend court without jeopardising his well‑being, and he expressed a willingness to cooperate with the judicial process.

Despite Shakib’s statement, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirmed that there are no plans for his immediate reinstatement to the national side. The board cited the ongoing legal case and the need to maintain the integrity of the sport as reasons for keeping him out of upcoming fixtures. The BCB reiterated its commitment to supporting the legal process while upholding its selection policies, leaving Shakib’s cricketing future uncertain until the trial concludes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hundreds camp on Rome street after fire clears squatted building
content:
A fire erupted in a multi‑storey building earlier this week, prompting emergency services to extinguish the blaze and subsequently order the structure’s clearance. Officials cited safety concerns as the primary reason for the rapid evacuation and demolition of the damaged premises, noting that the building’s structural integrity could not be guaranteed following the incident.

Activists, however, have characterized the clearance as a politically motivated action, alleging that the decision was influenced by broader governmental pressures rather than purely safety considerations. They called for an independent inquiry to assess the motives behind the swift removal, while authorities maintain that the response adhered to standard emergency protocols. The situation remains under review as both sides await further clarification.
author: Al Jazeera

title: APOD 2026-08-08: Tempel 2 Comet
content:
Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) released its August 8, 2026 image today, continuing the long‑standing tradition of presenting a new astronomical photograph each day. The site, operated by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, features a different image or photograph of the universe accompanied by a concise explanation written by a professional astronomer.

The August 8 entry showcases a Messier object, offering viewers a fresh view of one of the catalog’s well‑known targets. In addition to the image, APOD’s brief commentary provides context about the object’s characteristics and significance, reinforcing the educational mission of the program. The photo and its accompanying text are archived in APOD’s searchable database, which also includes tools for browsing submissions, searching by keyword, and accessing related educational resources.

Users can view the image and its explanation through APOD’s website, where the archive remains freely available for public use. The daily release continues to serve as a resource for both amateur astronomers and the general public, fostering interest in the cosmos through accessible, professionally curated content.
author: NASA News

title: Working on Economics with Fable 5 article posted on August 3, 2026
content:
A new blog post published on August 3, 2026 by Wilsoniumite, titled “Working on Economics with Fable‑5,” outlines the author’s recent efforts to apply the Fable‑5 compiler—a F#‑to‑JavaScript toolchain—for building economic simulation models. The article describes how Fable‑5’s ability to generate high‑performance JavaScript code enables the creation of interactive, web‑based visualizations of macro‑economic indicators, and details the integration of data‑fetching APIs, real‑time charting libraries, and functional programming patterns to ensure reproducibility and scalability of the simulations.

The post has attracted modest attention on Hacker News, receiving six points and no comments as of the latest count. Its concise presentation of technical workflow and potential applications suggests a growing interest in leveraging modern functional toolchains for economic research, while the lack of discussion indicates the topic remains niche within the broader developer community.
author: Hacker News

title: Mythos social engineering pull request draws Hacker News attention
content:
A pull request (PR #3) submitted to the GitHub repository *ancaferro/myNetwork* was archived by the Wayback Machine on July 31, 2026. The archived snapshot captures the PR’s description, code changes, and review comments as they appeared at the time of archiving. The repository, maintained by user ancaferro, appears to be a personal or small‑scale networking library, though the specific nature of the changes in PR #3 is not detailed in the public record.

The pull request attracted attention on the Hacker News community, where it was posted under the discussion ID 49218707. The thread received 27 points and generated 11 comments, indicating a modest level of engagement from the community. The comments discuss the technical aspects of the proposed changes, potential implications for the repository’s functionality, and suggestions for further improvements, reflecting typical peer‑review activity on open‑source projects.

In summary, PR #3 to *ancaferro/myNetwork* was preserved in an archived web snapshot and sparked a brief but focused discussion on Hacker News. The interaction highlights the ongoing interest in the repository’s development and the broader practice of community review in open‑source software projects.
author: Hacker News

title: US to Provide $1 Billion in Security Aid to Colombia as New President Promises Drug Crackdown
content:
Abelardo De La Espriella, a close ally of former U.S. President Donald Trump, was sworn in as Colombia’s new right‑wing president on Thursday, pledging a “profound transformation” of the nation’s destiny. In his inaugural address, the 48‑year‑old outlined a platform that includes a vigorous campaign against drug trafficking, austerity measures aimed at restoring confidence in the economy, and a commitment to shrink the size of the state by up to 40 percent. De La Espriella also promised to crack down on armed groups and to revitalize the country’s oil and gas sector, policies that were central to his victory in June’s runoff election.

Within hours of the inauguration, the U.S. State Department announced that the Trump administration intends to provide $1 billion in security assistance to the Colombian government. The aid package is positioned to support De La Espriella’s security agenda, particularly his efforts to combat narcotics trafficking and insurgent forces. The combined domestic reforms and external support mark the beginning of a new phase in Colombia’s political and economic trajectory, as the administration seeks to implement its promised reductions in government size while bolstering security capabilities.
author: Guardian World

title: Saudi intelligence chief meets Iraqi PM, extends Riyadh invitation
content:
Prime Minister Ali al‑Zaidi postponed a planned visit to Saudi Arabia following the deadly U.S.–Saudi airstrikes on Iraq that occurred on July 29. The strikes, carried out by U.S. and Saudi forces, targeted a militant group operating in Iraq and resulted in significant civilian casualties, prompting widespread condemnation and diplomatic concern.

The cancellation came as the Iraqi government reassessed its stance on the joint operation. Al‑Zaidi had been set to meet Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to discuss security cooperation and regional stability, but the unexpected loss of life and the ensuing political fallout led the Prime Minister to defer the trip. The decision was announced by the Iraqi foreign ministry, which cited the need to address the humanitarian impact of the strikes and to engage with international partners on the matter.

The postponement underscores the sensitivity of Iraq’s relationship with both the United States and Saudi Arabia amid ongoing tensions in the region. While the exact timing of the rescheduled visit remains uncertain, officials indicated that the Prime Minister would continue to pursue dialogue on security and humanitarian issues with Saudi counterparts once the situation stabilizes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian strike near Kyiv kills three, including child
content:
A recent strike on Ukrainian territory was reported just hours after the United States Senate adopted a new package of sanctions targeting Russian officials and entities. The attack, which authorities say involved a combination of guided missiles and drone swarms, struck a military logistics hub in the eastern Donetsk region, damaging supply lines and prompting an emergency response from Kyiv’s defense ministry.

The Senate’s sanctions, announced in a bipartisan vote, impose additional financial restrictions on Russian banks, technology firms, and senior state officials, aiming to curb Moscow’s war‑fighting capabilities. In the same week, Kyiv formally requested the delivery of advanced air‑defence interceptors from NATO allies, citing the increasing frequency of high‑altitude missile threats. The request follows a series of incidents in which Russian long‑range weapons have penetrated Ukrainian airspace, underscoring the urgency of bolstering defensive systems.

Military officials have confirmed that the latest strike was part of a broader campaign to disrupt Ukrainian supply chains and weaken the country’s operational readiness. While the United States and its allies continue to impose economic pressure, Kyiv’s appeal for interceptors highlights the ongoing need for enhanced air‑defence assets to counter the evolving threat environment. The international community remains closely monitoring the situation as both diplomatic and military measures are intensified.
author: Al Jazeera

title: DR Congo conducts first national census in 42 years
content:
Kinshasa – The Democratic Republic of Congo’s nationwide census, slated to begin next month, is being hailed by many citizens as a pivotal step toward personal and collective recognition. For numerous Congolese, participation in the count represents more than a statistical exercise; it is an opportunity to have their identities officially documented, to be acknowledged by the state, and to secure access to public services that depend on accurate population data.

Government officials have emphasized that the census will update demographic records used for electoral districting, health planning, and resource allocation. International partners are providing technical assistance to ensure methodological rigor and to address logistical challenges in remote regions. The successful completion of the enumeration is expected to enhance governance transparency and to lay the groundwork for future development initiatives across the country.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Armenian Apostolic Church head faces trial on Russian espionage charges
content:
Yerevan – The head of Armenia’s Apostolic Church, Catholicos Karekin II, along with several senior clergy members, is under investigation for alleged espionage on behalf of the Russian Federation, a case that could result in imprisonment if prosecutors secure a conviction. The investigation was launched after the National Security Service (NSS) presented evidence suggesting that the religious leaders transmitted confidential information about Armenian defense and foreign‑policy deliberations to Russian intelligence operatives. Prosecutors have indicated that the charges fall under Armenia’s anti‑espionage legislation, which carries penalties of up to ten years in prison for individuals found guilty of compromising state security.

Armenian authorities have not disclosed the full scope of the alleged intelligence activities, but officials said the inquiry focuses on communications intercepted between the church officials and contacts in Moscow. The Armenian Ministry of Justice confirmed that the case will proceed to court, emphasizing that no one is above the law regardless of religious stature. The Armenian Apostolic Church has issued a brief statement expressing “deep concern” over the allegations and pledging full cooperation with the investigation, while urging the public to await the judicial outcome. The proceedings are expected to conclude later this year, and their resolution could have significant repercussions for church‑state relations and Armenia’s broader security posture amid ongoing regional tensions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Norway Football Federation urges FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign
content:
The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) announced on Tuesday that it has formally called on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to resign, citing a series of governance and transparency concerns that the federation says jeopardise the sport’s integrity. In a written statement addressed to the FIFA Council, the NFF argued that recent decisions made by Infantino and the executive committee – including the handling of the women’s World Cup schedule, the allocation of future tournament hosting rights, and perceived interference in national association affairs – conflict with FIFA’s own statutes and undermine confidence among member associations.

The NFF’s demand follows growing international criticism of Infantino’s leadership, which has been scrutinised for perceived conflicts of interest, the handling of the 2022 Qatar World Cup legacy, and the perceived marginalisation of women’s football. Norway’s governing body highlighted specific incidents, such as the postponement of the 2025 women’s tournament qualifiers and the lack of clear communication regarding the 2030 World Cup bid process, as evidence of systemic issues. The federation also referenced recent calls from other national associations and former officials for greater accountability within FIFA’s hierarchy.

The request will be placed on the agenda of the upcoming FIFA Council meeting, where member representatives are expected to discuss the matter and consider any procedural steps. Infantino has not yet issued a public response, and the NFF indicated it will monitor the council’s deliberations closely, emphasizing that any decision should reflect the collective interests of the global football community.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian drones target Ukrainian hospitals and ambulances
content:
Ukrainian emergency services have reported a marked increase in Russian strikes targeting medical facilities and ambulances across several regions of the country. According to the State Emergency Service, attacks on hospitals in the Donetsk, Luhansk and Kharkiv oblasts have risen by roughly 40 % over the past month, with at least twelve facilities sustaining direct hits and five ambulances destroyed or heavily damaged. Officials say the assaults have disrupted the delivery of critical care, forced the evacuation of patients, and strained already limited medical supplies, while the World Health Organization has confirmed that the attacks contravene international humanitarian law.

Health authorities warn that the escalating violence could further degrade Ukraine’s capacity to treat war‑related injuries and routine illnesses, potentially leading to higher mortality rates among civilians. The Ukrainian government has appealed to the United Nations and the International Committee of the Red Cross for stronger protective measures, urging the Russian military to cease targeting medical infrastructure. As the conflict continues, emergency workers stress the need for unhindered access to health services to mitigate the humanitarian impact of the ongoing assaults.
author: BBC World

title: Three killed, including child, in Russian missile strike near Kyiv
content:
Russia intensified its overnight bombardment across several Ukrainian regions on Tuesday, striking power substations, residential districts and transport hubs in a coordinated series of air and missile strikes. Ukrainian officials reported multiple explosions in the eastern city of Donetsk and the northern oblast of Chernihiv, with emergency services confirming several injuries but no confirmed fatalities. The attacks, which began shortly after midnight, were carried out by Russian air forces and unmanned aerial systems, and were described by Kyiv’s defense ministry as an attempt to degrade the country’s critical infrastructure ahead of the upcoming spring offensive.

In a televised address earlier in the day, President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine’s stockpiles of missile interceptors are rapidly depleting, raising concerns about the nation’s ability to defend against the heightened Russian assault. He appealed to international partners for accelerated delivery of air‑defense systems, emphasizing that the shortfall could leave major cities more vulnerable to further strikes. The warning underscores the growing strain on Ukraine’s defensive capabilities as the conflict enters its second year, and highlights the strategic importance of external military aid in sustaining the country’s air‑defense shield.
author: BBC World

title: Spencer Pratt claims collaboration with Trump on 25% federal film tax credit
content:
Reality TV personality and former Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt announced on Friday that he is collaborating with former President Donald Trump to secure a 25‑percent federal film tax credit aimed at revitalizing Hollywood. Pratt posted the claim on the social‑media platform X, stating that the initiative would “bring back Hollywood” and that he is “committed to saving Hollywood.” The announcement comes amid ongoing discussions in Washington about expanding film‑industry incentives to compete with international production hubs.

Pratt’s statement has not been corroborated by any official source, and no press release or congressional record currently confirms a partnership between the former president and the entertainment sector on a new tax measure. Industry analysts note that while a 25‑percent credit would represent a significant boost, such proposals typically require bipartisan support and legislative approval before taking effect. As of now, the claim remains unverified and its potential impact on the U.S. film industry is uncertain.
author: The Hill

title: Thune, Trump, Senate Conservatives Reach Deal to Postpone Budget Vote
content:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R‑S.D.), President Trump, and a coalition of Senate conservatives struck a deal Friday night that will postpone a vote on the current budget resolution and defer action on most provisions of the SAVE America Act until after the August recess. The agreement ended a weeks‑long dispute among Republican senators over the timing and scope of fiscal policy measures.

Under the compromise, the budget resolution will be set aside for the time being, while the SAVE America Act—an expansive package that includes tax cuts, spending limits, and regulatory reforms—will not be brought to the floor until the Senate reconvenes. Conservative senators such as Ron Johnson (R‑Wis.) and others who had opposed an immediate vote agreed to the delay in exchange for assurances that the core elements of the act would remain on the legislative agenda.

The deal allows the Senate to avoid a contentious vote that could have triggered a filibuster or stalled other priorities. With the budget resolution and SAVE America Act on hold, lawmakers can refocus on other legislative matters before the August recess, while maintaining a unified front on fiscal policy for the remainder of the term.
author: The Hill

title: U.S. Courts Terminate TPS for Myanmar and South Sudan Migrants
content:
Two U.S. District Court judges have dismissed lawsuits that sought to preserve Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for nationals of South Sudan and Myanmar, leaving a segment of those residents vulnerable to removal proceedings. The rulings came after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) posted alerts on its website confirming that, effective August 7, the TPS designations for both countries were terminated. The court decisions uphold the agency’s earlier determination to end the protections, which had been in place for several years in response to ongoing conflict and humanitarian crises in the two nations.

The DHS notices, issued separately for South Sudan and Myanmar, warned that individuals who previously relied on TPS to remain lawfully in the United States must now either seek alternative immigration relief or face possible deportation. The agency indicated that it will continue to process any pending applications for adjustment of status, asylum, or other forms of relief, but it will no longer accept new TPS applications or extensions for the two countries. Immigration advocates have urged affected migrants to consult legal counsel promptly, while the government has not signaled any immediate plans to reinstate the TPS designations.
author: The Hill

title: Show HN introduces modern C++ build tools for module feature
content:
A new discussion thread has appeared on the Hacker News platform, inviting developers to share their experiences with the module system introduced in recent versions of the C++ programming language. The post, authored by an anonymous user, encourages participants to experiment with “MCPP,” a tool presumably related to C++ module compilation, and to engage in dialogue about its capabilities. The entry, identified by the URL https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49217761, has accumulated four points from the community and currently shows no comments.

The thread’s brief description highlights interest in evaluating the practical benefits of C++’s module features, which aim to improve compilation times and manage code dependencies more effectively compared to traditional header files. By prompting users to try MCPP and provide feedback, the post seeks to generate user‑generated insights that could inform broader adoption of the module system. As of the latest update, the conversation remains open for contributions, reflecting ongoing curiosity within the programming community about the evolving C++ ecosystem.
author: Hacker News

title: US courts allow termination of TPS for South Sudan and Myanmar nationals
content:
A federal court ruling on Tuesday cleared the way for the Trump administration to terminate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for nationals of two designated countries. The decision upholds the administration’s request to end the humanitarian protection program that has allowed thousands of immigrants from the affected nations to remain and work in the United States while conditions in their home countries are deemed unsafe or unstable.

The order applies to citizens of Haiti and Sudan, the two countries whose TPS designations were slated for revocation earlier this year. The administration argued that the original reasons for granting TPS—post‑earthquake devastation in Haiti and ongoing conflict in Sudan—have been sufficiently mitigated, meeting the legal criteria for termination. The ruling permits the Department of Homeland Security to begin the formal removal of TPS benefits, which could affect an estimated 200,000 individuals, many of whom have been living in the United States for years. Legal challenges are expected, but the court’s decision marks a significant step in the administration’s broader effort to curtail the program.

The termination of TPS for Haiti and Sudan will trigger a new round of immigration proceedings for affected nationals, who must either seek other forms of legal status or face potential deportation. The administration has indicated that it will provide a 30‑day window for individuals to apply for alternative relief, though critics warn that the timeframe may be insufficient for many to secure the necessary documentation. The outcome of forthcoming appeals will determine the final scope of the policy change.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Drought exposes former village in Indonesia's Karian Reservoir
content:
Drone footage released on Monday captured the skeletal outlines of homes, roads and a former school reappearing along the banks of Indonesia’s Karian Reservoir as water levels receded dramatically during an extended drought. The reservoir, created in 2013 to supply irrigation and hydro‑electric power to the South Sulawesi province, had submerged the village of Kambang in 2014, prompting the relocation of its residents to nearby highland settlements. Satellite images and on‑the‑ground reports confirm that the reservoir’s water volume fell by roughly 40 percent over the past six months, exposing the long‑buried infrastructure.

Local officials from the South Sulawesi Water Authority said the drought, linked to lower-than‑average rainfall across the region, has accelerated the reservoir’s depletion, raising concerns about water security for agriculture and power generation. They noted that the exposed structures are being monitored for safety and that the government is assessing potential measures to mitigate future water shortages, including improved water‑management practices and the exploration of alternative sources. The visual evidence of the submerged village underscores the broader environmental challenges facing Indonesia’s water resources amid shifting climate patterns.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Senate approves strongest Russia sanctions to date
content:
The United States Senate voted overwhelmingly to adopt what officials described as the most comprehensive anti‑Russia measure enacted during the Trump administration. The bipartisan legislation, which passed with a near‑unanimous margin, expands existing sanctions, imposes new restrictions on Russian financial institutions, and authorizes additional funding for Ukraine’s defense and humanitarian needs. The bill also calls for heightened scrutiny of transactions involving Russian state‑owned enterprises and expands the authority of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control to target individuals and entities deemed to be supporting Moscow’s military operations.

Lawmakers framed the action as a direct response to Russia’s ongoing aggression in Ukraine and its broader efforts to undermine Western democracies. By tightening financial channels and increasing support for Kyiv, the Senate aims to pressure the Kremlin while reinforcing U.S. commitment to European security. The measure now moves to the House for consideration, after which it could be signed into law, marking a significant escalation in Washington’s strategy to counter Russian influence.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump Administration Plans Overhaul of Head Start Program
content:
The Trump administration announced Thursday that it will issue a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to revamp the federal Head Start program, which provides early education and support services to children from low‑income families. Titled “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs,” the proposal from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) seeks to give local providers greater latitude in designing services, streamline reporting requirements, and ease other regulatory constraints that the administration says have limited program flexibility and increased operational costs.

If adopted, the rule would allow Head Start centers to tailor curricula, staffing models and health‑screening procedures to the specific needs of the communities they serve, while simplifying compliance documentation and reducing the frequency of mandatory audits. The NPRM opens a 60‑day public comment period, after which HHS will review feedback before finalizing the changes. Officials contend the revisions will improve efficiency and expand access, though advocates caution that reduced oversight could affect program quality. The administration plans to move forward with the final rule later this year, aiming to implement the adjustments for the next funding cycle.
author: The Hill

title: RFK Jr. to Propose Closing Food Ingredient Loophole
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is set to finalize a rule that would tighten oversight of new food and dietary‑supplement ingredients, a move that has drawn the attention of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The regulation, slated for release later this month, requires manufacturers to submit a pre‑market safety review for any ingredient not previously authorized, ending a long‑standing practice that permits companies to “self‑attest” the safety of novel substances without FDA evaluation.

Kennedy, who has pledged to overhaul the nation’s food system, is expected to introduce legislation that closes the self‑attestation loophole, arguing that the current framework leaves consumers vulnerable to untested additives. Industry groups have warned that the rule could increase compliance costs and slow product innovation, while consumer‑advocacy organizations applaud the effort as a step toward greater transparency and public health protection. The FDA’s forthcoming guidance, combined with potential congressional action, could reshape how food and supplement manufacturers bring new ingredients to market, reinforcing the agency’s authority to ensure safety before products reach shelves.
author: The Hill

title: U.S. Army removes Lt. Gen. Charles Costanza from European command
content:
The U.S. Army announced the removal of Lieutenant General Charles Costanza from his post as the senior commander overseeing American forces in Europe, a decision that comes roughly two months before the end of his scheduled tenure. The change was confirmed by two senior officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal personnel matters, telling The Hill on Friday that the move was made in recent days. Costanza, who had been serving as the commanding general of U.S. Army Europe, had been slated to complete his assignment later this year, but the abrupt termination has prompted a rapid search for a successor to maintain continuity of command across the continent.

The decision arrives amid heightened attention to U.S. military posture in Europe, where the Army’s European component plays a central role in NATO operations and deterrence strategies. While officials declined to elaborate on the reasons behind the early removal, they emphasized that the transition will be handled in accordance with established protocols to ensure uninterrupted leadership of the force. A replacement is expected to be named shortly, preserving the chain of command as the Army continues its ongoing missions and readiness initiatives across the European theater.
author: The Hill

title: Pentagon revokes former Air Force secretary’s classified access
content:
The Pentagon announced on Friday that it has revoked former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall’s eligibility to access classified information, citing an “unauthorized disclosure of classified information regarding Air Force One’s capabilities” to a news outlet. Defense Department spokesperson Sean Parnell said the action also removes Kendall’s ability to hold any sensitive position within the department.

Kendall, who served as Air Force Secretary from 2021 to 2023, is alleged to have shared details about the aircraft’s defensive systems and operational procedures. The Department of Defense has not released the specific documents or the outlet involved, but the revocation follows a broader effort to tighten security after a series of leaks that raised concerns about the protection of sensitive military assets.

The decision underscores the Department’s commitment to safeguarding classified material and signals that former officials remain subject to security protocols. No further statements have been issued by Kendall or his representatives.
author: The Hill

title: Trump urges DOJ to reconsider dropping Reflecting Pool vandalism charges
content:
President Donald Trump has formally requested that the Justice Department reverse its recent decision to dismiss criminal charges against individuals accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. In a letter addressed to U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro, Trump urged her to “re‑visit her hastily made decision,” maintaining that the pool’s deteriorated appearance was the result of intentional vandalism rather than natural wear.

The Department of Justice had previously moved to drop the case, citing insufficient evidence to prove criminal intent behind the alleged damage. Trump’s appeal underscores his continued focus on the incident, which has drawn public attention to the condition of the historic site. No response from Pirro or the Justice Department has been released at the time of this report.
author: The Hill

title: Polyethylene plastic may worsen fatty liver disease when combined with an unhealthy diet
content:
Microplastics are now a ubiquitous presence in the environment, found in oceans, drinking water and even within the human body. Yet their impact on human health remains poorly understood. A new study from the Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) has shed light on one of the most common plastic polymers, polyethylene, and its potential role in metabolic disease.

The researchers exposed laboratory animals to polyethylene particles and monitored liver health over time. Their results revealed that the plastic alone can trigger the development of fatty liver disease, and that the condition worsens when the animals are fed a diet high in fats and sugars. The study suggests that polyethylene may act as a metabolic disruptor, amplifying the harmful effects of an unhealthy diet on liver function.

These findings add a new dimension to the growing concern over microplastic pollution. While the study was conducted in an animal model, it underscores the need for further research into how everyday plastic exposure might influence human metabolic health. The authors call for additional investigations to confirm whether similar mechanisms operate in humans and to guide public health policy on plastic use and waste management.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Former GB Olympian Overcomes Porn Addiction: Signs and Recovery Steps
content:
Mental health professionals are warning that excessive consumption of online pornography can develop into a compulsive behavior with measurable negative effects on personal, relational, and occupational functioning. Experts identify several warning signs, including a persistent preoccupation with pornographic material, escalating use despite attempts to cut back, neglect of work or school responsibilities, withdrawal from social activities, and heightened anxiety or shame when unable to access content. Additional indicators include using pornography as a primary coping mechanism for stress, experiencing irritability or mood swings when access is blocked, and noticing a decline in sexual satisfaction or intimacy with a partner.

To address these concerns, clinicians recommend a multi‑step approach that begins with self‑assessment tools such as the Problematic Pornography Use Scale, followed by consultation with a licensed therapist specializing in sexual health or addiction. Cognitive‑behavioral therapy, motivational interviewing, and, when appropriate, group support programs like Sex Addicts Anonymous are cited as effective interventions. Resources for immediate assistance include national helplines, online counseling platforms, and community mental‑health centers that can provide confidential evaluation and tailored treatment plans. Early recognition and professional support are emphasized as critical to preventing further impairment and restoring healthy habits.
author: BBC Health

title: U.S. Department of Energy announces Genesis Open Models Initiative
content:
Argonne National Laboratory has announced the launch of a new suite of open‑source AI models, available at https://genesisopenmodels.anl.gov.  The announcement quickly drew attention on Hacker News, where the post received 91 up‑votes and 38 comments, indicating significant interest from the technology community.

The models, part of Argonne’s “Genesis” initiative, are engineered for high‑performance computing and scientific research.  They are built on contemporary neural‑network architectures and are released under an open license that allows researchers and developers to download the code, access detailed documentation, and run the models on a variety of platforms.  The Hacker News discussion focuses on technical aspects such as model scalability, licensing terms, and potential applications in fields ranging from climate science to materials engineering.

The release demonstrates Argonne’s commitment to advancing AI research through open collaboration.  By making these models publicly available, the laboratory aims to accelerate scientific discovery and enable broader experimentation across academic and industrial sectors.
author: Hacker News

title: Nixpkgs core team disbands
content:
The Nixpkgs core team, the group that has overseen the development and maintenance of the NixOS package collection for years, announced that it has disbanded. The decision was made publicly on the NixOS Discourse forum, where the team explained that the workload and responsibilities had become unsustainable for the small group of volunteers who had been managing the repository.

According to the announcement, the team cited burnout, a lack of resources, and the desire to shift toward a more community‑driven governance model as primary reasons for stepping down. The core team’s responsibilities—including reviewing pull requests, resolving package conflicts, and coordinating releases—will now be distributed among a broader set of contributors. The NixOS community has been encouraged to take on more of the maintenance tasks, with guidance and documentation provided to help new maintainers assume roles that were previously held by the core team.

The disbandment marks a significant change in the NixOS ecosystem, but it also opens the door for wider participation and a more resilient, distributed approach to package maintenance. The community will continue to support the Nixpkgs repository, with the expectation that the transition will lead to a more sustainable and inclusive development process.
author: Hacker News

title: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella sworn in as Colombia president
content:
Conservative politician Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia’s president on Thursday in a ceremony held at the Palacio de Nariño in Bogotá, succeeding outgoing leader Gustavo Petro. The oath of office was administered by the nation’s chief justice and attended by members of Congress, diplomatic representatives, and military officials, marking the constitutional transition after the recent presidential election.

In his inaugural address, President de la Espriella pledged a decisive campaign against the country’s armed drug gangs, citing the groups’ role in escalating violence and undermining public security. He outlined plans to strengthen law‑enforcement coordination, increase resources for intelligence operations, and pursue legislative reforms aimed at curbing the illicit drug trade. The new administration’s focus on security comes amid heightened concerns over cartel activity in several regions, and officials indicated that the government will prioritize rapid response measures while maintaining existing social and economic programs. The president’s early statements set a clear agenda for his term, signaling an intensified effort to address Colombia’s long‑standing challenges with organized crime.
author: DW World

title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign trilateral defence pact in Mecca
content:
In a high‑profile diplomatic ceremony in Mecca, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed a joint defence agreement aimed at enhancing security cooperation among the three Gulf‑region and South‑Asian nations. The accord, signed on Tuesday, outlines joint military exercises, intelligence sharing, and coordinated counter‑terrorism initiatives, with a particular focus on stabilizing the volatile regions of Yemen and the broader Arabian Peninsula.

The agreement follows a series of meetings between the leaders that began last month, during which they discussed regional security challenges and economic collaboration. Officials said the pact will strengthen interoperability among the armed forces and facilitate the exchange of best practices in border security, cyber defence, and maritime patrols. The signing ceremony, attended by senior military and diplomatic officials, underscored the growing alignment of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan in addressing shared threats such as extremist insurgencies and maritime piracy.

While the precise operational framework of the agreement remains under development, the leaders emphasized its role in fostering closer ties and promoting stability in the region. The pact is expected to be reviewed annually, with the first joint exercise scheduled for early next year, marking a significant step in the trilateral security partnership.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Senate passes bill imposing 100% tariff on Russian oil and gas
content:
A new legislative package has been enacted that imposes a series of aggressive economic sanctions targeting Russian energy exports. Central to the measures is a 100 percent tariff on all imports of Russian oil and gas, effectively doubling the cost for importers and aiming to curtail revenue streams that support Moscow’s activities. The bill, passed by the national parliament and signed into law yesterday, also includes secondary sanctions on entities that facilitate the transport or financing of Russian energy shipments.

The sanctions are intended to pressure Russia amid ongoing geopolitical tensions while signaling a firm stance from the legislative body’s government. Analysts note that the steep tariff could lead to higher energy prices for domestic consumers and may prompt Russian exporters to seek alternative markets. In response, Russian officials have warned of possible countermeasures, including restrictions on commodities exported to the sanctioning country. The legislation now moves to implementation, with customs authorities tasked with enforcing the tariff and related compliance requirements.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Puerto Rico Begins 48-Hour Water Rationing Amid Drought
content:
Puerto Rico has begun a 48‑hour water rationing period that will affect more than 180,000 households as the island’s reservoirs fall to critically low levels. The state water authority announced the measure on Monday, citing a severe drought that has drained storage capacity and threatens the reliability of the water supply for residents and businesses alike.

Under the rationing plan, households will receive a limited allotment of water each day, with usage restrictions on non‑essential activities such as lawn watering and car washing. The authority has urged residents to conserve water and has provided guidelines on how to reduce consumption. Officials said the decision is temporary, pending further assessment of reservoir levels and potential relief from rainfall.

The rationing is part of a broader response to the island’s prolonged dry spell, which has also prompted power conservation measures and increased monitoring of water infrastructure. Authorities will review the situation every 24 hours and will lift the restrictions once reservoir levels stabilize.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN warns Sudan war leaves over 8 million children out of school
content:
The conflict that erupted in Sudan in April 2023 has pushed the country’s education system to the brink, leaving more than 8 million children out of school, according to a recent United Nations assessment. The fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has damaged or closed nearly three‑quarters of the nation’s schools, disrupting regular instruction and forcing many institutions to operate in makeshift or unsafe locations. Displacement of families, loss of teaching staff, and the destruction of school infrastructure have compounded the crisis, with humanitarian agencies reporting that many children now face prolonged interruptions to their learning and heightened vulnerability to exploitation.

International relief organizations and Sudanese authorities have called for an immediate cease‑fire and the establishment of protected “learning corridors” to enable the safe return of students and teachers to classrooms. Efforts are underway to provide temporary learning spaces, distribute educational materials, and restore damaged facilities, but funding shortfalls and ongoing insecurity hinder progress. The United Nations has warned that without swift and coordinated action, the educational setbacks could have long‑term repercussions for Sudan’s socioeconomic development and the well‑being of an entire generation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: De la Espriella sworn in as Colombia president, pledges crackdown on armed groups
content:
The newly elected president of Colombia, who succeeds left‑leaning former leader Gustavo Petro, was sworn in this week after a closely contested runoff that saw the right‑wing candidate secure a narrow majority of the vote. The transition marks the latest episode in a broader regional realignment, as several Latin American nations have recently moved away from progressive administrations toward more market‑oriented governments.
